newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African police revise mine death toll down to 32.
newsitem.headline: S.African police revise mine death toll down to 32.

text.p: South African police said on Tuesday the death toll from ethnic clashes near a platinum mine northwest of Johannesburg at the weekend had been established as 32, not 37 as they had first reported.
"There was a mistake with the figures. It's 32," police spokeswoman Captain Belinda Kleynhans told Reuters.
She said the situation was calm on Tuesday, with no further violence reported since Sunday. Police patrols were scaled down on Monday but some police would remain as a precaution.
Police said fighting between members of different tribes broke out on Saturday morning at a squatter camp called Freedom Park near the Wildebeesfontein mine in Rustenburg.
The clashes, between members of the Sotho and Xhosa tribes, spread to a hostel for migrant workers at the mine, owned by Impala Platinum Holdings.
South Africa's National Union of Mineworkers', the largest in the industry, has condemned the ethnic feuding on mines and has vowed to help identify the culprits.
The industry is built on a labour system under which men left their wives and families for months at a time to work on the mines. Mine hostels were largely segregated on ethnic lines.
